lines.text: Every month, a founder proves their own numbers at eleven o'clock. No controller. No finance team. This is the close when nobody is left to do it.

So we handed it the books. Seapoint MCP, live — accounts, transactions, invoices, read with my own permissions. One question: a hundred and sixty-two thousand pounds of September spend, twelve categories. But asking isn't the point. Watch what happens when nobody asks.

Of two thousand six hundred and sixty-four transactions, two thousand six hundred and twenty-nine reconcile themselves. Fourteen need a human. Point five per cent. Everything else it files quietly: classify, generate, verify, repair. What the human gets isn't a wall of output — fourteen lines, each with a reason and its evidence.

Then I confirm. Connolly Accountants, eighteen hundred pounds, receipt attached, vendor unambiguous. The decision is recorded before anything is written; needs-review becomes awaiting-approval. Nothing on the ledger moves without me.

And this is the one I'd show a partner. Meridian Insurance, twelve hundred and forty. Filed as legal fees, coded as insurance, no receipt. Two hundred and forty-eight pounds of VAT rides on which one is right. A tired founder rubber-stamps it. close-keeper won't fill the cell. It shows me the contradiction instead.

Everyone in AI accounting sells you accuracy. Ninety-seven point eight per cent, taken on faith. We sell the point five per cent it won't take on faith. Enterprise close software needs a controller and a hundred and fifty thousand a year. A twelve-person startup has neither. close-keeper.
